title: Generic triviality of a line module over a valuation base with integral geometric fibres
statement: Let $R$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a proper flat finitely presented morphism from an algebraic space [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation also includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. A geometric fibre is a base change to the spectrum of an algebraically closed field; integral means nonempty, reduced and irreducible. A line module means a module on the small etale structure sheaf locally isomorphic to that structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]; on a scheme it corresponds to an ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose every geometric fibre of $f$ is integral. If a line module $L$ on $X$ has $L|_{X_K}\simeq\mathcal O_{X_K}$, then $L\simeq\mathcal O_X$. The valuation ring may have arbitrary rank and need not be Noetherian; neither a section nor a rigidification nor an algebraic Picard space is assumed. Direct image and tensor pullback are the canonical functors on small etale module sheaves [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

source.place: Tag 0DNJ, lemma-pic-functor-uniqueness-part, proof from the paragraph beginning Denote f through the final trivialization: the valuation-ring line-module argument, rather than the separatedness conclusion

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, let $\eta$ and $0$ be its generic and closed points, and put $L^{-1}=\mathcal H om(L,\mathcal O_X)$. On a trivializing etale chart, $L$ and $L^{-1}$ are the structure module, hence quasi-coherent of finite presentation and flat over $R$, since $f$ is flat. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] separately to them. This gives perfect Zariski complexes $E=K_f(L)$ and $E^-=K_f(L^{-1})$, and canonical identifications of their derived fibres with the corresponding fibre cohomology, for ordinary and geometric residue fields. There is no Noetherian or rank-one-valuation assumption.

source.place: Tag 0DNJ, lemma-pic-functor-uniqueness-part, proof from Denote f to the final trivialization

proof.text: Choose algebraic closures of $K$ and $\kappa(0)$. The geometric generic fibre is proper integral, and $L$ and $L^{-1}$ are trivial on it. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-field-global-functions] its structure sheaf has a one-dimensional space of sections. Hence $\beta_{E,0}(\eta)=\beta_{E^-,0}(\eta)=1$, using the fibre identifications of step 1 and field-extension invariance in [lem-sc-perfect-jump-loci]. By upper semicontinuity in that same node, both dimensions at $0$ are at least one: the closed set $\{\beta\ge1\}$ contains $\eta$, hence its closure $T$. After extending the closed residue field to its algebraic closure, both opposite line modules therefore have nonzero sections. Apply [lem-sfb-space-dual-effective-line-triviality] to this proper integral geometric closed fibre. Its restriction of $L$ is trivial. Applying the constants lemma again and invariance of fibre dimensions gives $\beta_{E,0}(0)=1$.

source.place: Tag 0DNJ, lemma-pic-functor-uniqueness-part, proof from Denote f to the final trivialization

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-module-preimage] and [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] to $E$ on $T$, obtaining its pseudo-coherent ring complex $C\in D(R)$ with finite Tor amplitude. The affine equivalence and the field-fibre identifications of step 1 identify $H^i(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\kappa(0))$ with $H^i(X_0,L_0)$; in particular these vanish for $i<0$. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-pseudocoherent-residue-model] with $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_R$ and $a=0$. Its localization element is outside the maximal ideal, hence is a unit, so the resulting bounded finite-free complex $P$ is over $R$ itself. It has no negative terms and $P^0=R$, since the residue dimension in degree zero is one. Termwise tensor computes every derived fibre by [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback], under the affine equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0DNJ, lemma-pic-functor-uniqueness-part, proof from Denote f to the final trivialization

proof.text: Write $d^0:R\to P^1$ as a column of elements of $R$. Since $P^{-1}=0$ and $H^0(P\otimes_R K)$ has dimension one, the linear map $d^0\otimes_R K$ has full one-dimensional kernel and is zero. Every entry of the column therefore maps to zero in $K$; the injection $R\hookrightarrow K$ makes every entry zero in $R$. Consequently $1\in P^0$ is a cycle and gives a class generating $H^0(P)=R$. The same cycle generates $H^0(P\otimes_R\kappa(0))$: its dimension is one and its degree-zero term is already one-dimensional, so its differential is zero. The affine equivalence of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] together with degree-zero [lem-sfb-space-affine-base-higher-image-sections] identifies the class with a section $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$. Canonical base change from [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-base-change] takes this class to $1\otimes1$, so the restriction $s_0$ is nonzero. Over the geometric closed fibre, where $L$ is trivial, it is a nonzero scalar section by [lem-sfb-space-proper-field-global-functions]. Thus it generates $L$ on that fibre.

source.place: Tag 0DNJ, lemma-pic-functor-uniqueness-part, proof from Denote f to the final trivialization

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the non-generator locus of $s$. On an etale chart trivializing $L$, it is the closed zero locus of the regular function representing $s$; multiplying by a transition unit preserves this locus, so these loci define a closed subset of $|X|$. The preceding geometric-fibre calculation gives $Z\cap|X_0|=\varnothing$: a residue value is zero if and only if it becomes zero after a field extension. Universal closedness of $f$, part of the hypothesis proper, implies $f(Z)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. A nonempty closed subset $V(I)$ of the spectrum of the local ring $R$ contains its maximal ideal (a proper ideal $I$ lies in that ideal). Thus $f(Z)$ must be empty. The section is a unit in every local trivialization and its inverse local functions agree on overlaps. They glue to the inverse of $s:\mathcal O_X\to L$, proving $L\simeq\mathcal O_X$.
